title: Wyldcraft Gardens — hybrid onramp: call notes & next actions
content:
High-level: Wyldcraft Gardens wants a hybrid onramp — most inference on their private DC (edge rack) but with seamless fallback to Redwood hosted during batch spikes. Customer team: CTO (Marla), Head of Ops (Ben), infra lead (Asha). Call 2026-03-10 recap and concrete next steps.

Primary goals / constraints (verbatim-ish):
- Keep PHI-free but inventory + customer preferences considered sensitive (internal policy).
- Must stay within their private VLAN for baseline traffic; bursts can call hosted API only with strict allowlist and consent.
- Latency SLO: 90th perc < 120ms for short conversational queries (avg seq len 80 tokens).
- Peak QPS: baseline 40 qps, bursts to 180 qps during batch returns windows (15-30m windows).
- Cost target: prefer model quantized to int8 if accuracy delta < 2% vs fp16 for their top 15 prompts.

Technical notes / gotchas we surfaced:
- Onprem hardware: 2x A40-ish equivalent per rack, shared across multiple services. They want model hosting on a dedicated node in that rack. Need to confirm exact GPU model + driver stack.
- Storage: dataset snapshots live on NFS that is occasionally flaky during maintenance windows. KV cache persistence needs a local SSD layer; otherwise warm-up costs blow latency.
- Network: egress to Redwood hosted passes through a corporate proxy (explicit allowlist required). Firewall change window only 1x/day at 0300 UTC — affects rollout schedule.
- Auth: Enterprise KMS (AWS KMS) for keys, but onprem environment is Azure stack. We suggested PKCS#11-compatible HSM integration or bring-your-own KMS gateway. They asked for a short design note.
- Telemetry: they will not ship raw request tokens to hosted path; need token-level cost and sampled traces only. Also retention limit 30d.

Model / infra tradeoffs discussed:
- Candidate models: Redwood-verified small/medium causal models (13B quant) vs larger 33B fp16. For their latency and cost target, 13B/8bit looks promising.
- Batching: gentle batching with max latency budget 25ms per request — prefer continuous batching + per-customer KV cache.
- Fallback policy: route to hosted only when onprem utilization > 75% AND traffic type is idempotent (non-PHI). Need a routing flag from app layer to indicate 'safe for hosted'.

Action items (owner in parens):
- Asha: confirm exact GPU model + kernel driver versions; include NIC model (deadline 2026-03-15).
- Liam: draft short KMS/HSM integration options doc (PKCS11 vs KMS-gateway) and share with Wyldcraft security (deadline 2026-03-16).
- Priya: run a quick prompt-quality checkpoint (15 canonical prompts) on 13B int8 vs 33B fp16 and record BLEU/ROUGE-ish deltas; share results (deadline 2026-03-18).
- Sofia: propose rollout pad/schedule aligning firewall change window; propose canary plan with 3 hours rollback guard (deadline 2026-03-14).
- Dev: prepare a small demo repo showing: local KV cache warmup, fallback flag, and telemetry sample (deadline 2026-03-20).

Open questions for Wyldcraft (to clarify on follow-up):
- Can product add a "hosted-allowed" header on request to indicate data clearance? If not, we must infer from route and block tokens.
- Are there GDPR/CCPA-like obligations for the preference data store? Need legal confirmation to know whether metadata may leave onprem.
- SLA expectations if hosted fallback used — Wyldwood expects Redwood to accept responsibility for uptime for hosted portion during bursts? Need to map to contract.

Risks we flagged:
- Cache cold-starts (if KV not replicated to SSD) will cause token cost spikes on morning windows — propose pre-warm jobs.
- Proxy egress latency: corporate proxy occasionally adds 40-90ms; with 13B target this is a big % of tail. Consider co-locating a minimal edge-router to bypass corporate proxy just for fallback traffic (needs security sign-off).
- Model regression: if we quantize, top-n safety prompts must be regression-tested. Add to Redwood Optimize eval suite.

Quick rollout sketch (for internal use):
1) Spike: minimal container on their rack with 13B int8 + local SSD for KV, run 1 GPU, synthetic load test (2 days).
2) Pilot week: route 10% production but low-risk routes (returns inquiries) with wasm-based header that marks safe-to-fallback. Monitor latency, cost, prompt quality.
3) Expand: Increase onprem capacity (2 GPUs), enable auto-failover to hosted for non-sensitive traffic.

Notes / friction points to watch during execution:
- Firewall change window scheduling will likely push all canary work to early mornings — coordinate Ops.
- Their infra team is small; make the POC as turnkey as possible (scripted installer + preflight checks).
- Legal will likely require an annotation log for every fallback event (timestamp + route + samplingID).

Misc quick captures from the call (verbatim bullets):
- "We need to keep customer-facing PII locked on site — even feature flags mustn't exfil." — Marla
- "If we can get a 10–15% monthly unit-cost reduction vs their internal CPU baseline, they'll be happy." — Ben
- "We have an internal change freeze on last week of every month." — Ops note

Follow-up meeting: propose 2026-03-17 14:00 UTC for technical deep-dive. I'll draft agenda: 1) Asha: infra confirmations, 2) Liam: KMS options, 3) Priya: prompt QA results, 4) Demo run + telemetry.

End notes: Keep this doc light — will convert to a short client-facing one-pager after the 3/17 deep-dive. For now, this is the working locker for SE + Wyldcraft comms.
